transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brings me in is... I just can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. It's a mess. I work at a dry cleaner's, and lately, it's just tickets, receipts, workshop notes, customer jobs—all just piled together until I don't even know what to handle first. It's like looking at a mountain of paper. Speaking of mountains, my sister went to the Rockies last week. She sent me these pictures, and they were just gorgeous. I haven't been on a vacation in... gosh, it must be ten years. We used to go to the beach when the kids were little, but now everyone's so busy. My youngest is trying to start his own landscaping business, actually. He’s got a real green thumb, unlike me. I killed a cactus once. But anyway, yeah, the piles at work. I just... I look at them and my brain just kind of stops.
How long have you noticed these difficulties with staying organized and focused?

Well, it's really been causing me actual trouble for... I'd say about two years and two months now. That's right around when I started changing the business into this more complicated boutique model. Because, you know, regular dry cleaning is one thing, but boutique means we handle high-end stuff. Couture, delicate vintage pieces. I actually had this one lady bring in a 1920s flapper dress last month, and the beading on it was just incredible. All hand-stitched glass beads. I don't know how anyone had the patience for that back then! 

People today just don't have patience, do they? Everybody wants everything in five minutes. They call it fast fashion. My niece buys all her clothes from those cheap websites on her phone and they just fall apart after one wash. It's a terrible waste, really. She brought me a sweater to try and fix once and the yarn was practically made of plastic. You can't even steam something like that without it melting. 

But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, the boutique model. Yeah, it just made everything so much more complicated with all the special care instructions and different solvents we have to track, and that's when the piles really started getting completely out of hand for me.
Did you experience similar problems with focus or disorganization when you were a child or in school?

Well, you know, it's funny you ask that, because... yes, actually. Even way back in grade school. My mother kept all my old report cards in this big cedar chest at the foot of her bed. It smelled so strongly of cedar, you know? I love that smell. It reminds me of the holidays. We used to get a real tree every year until my husband developed this terrible allergy to pine. He'd just sneeze and sneeze until his eyes swelled up. So we had to switch to an artificial one, which just isn't the same. It's pre-lit, which is nice because I hate stringing lights, they always get tangled. 

But, um, my report cards. Right. My teachers always wrote the same thing. They'd tell my mother I was bright, but just... scattered. I was always talking out of turn, losing my homework papers, and they constantly had to remind me to just finish what I was doing. I guess I've always been a bit like that, but it's just so much worse with the business now.
Do you often feel restless inside, or find it difficult to sit still without fidgeting?

Well, I don't know if I'd say I feel restless inside, exactly. I mean, I guess I do tap my foot a lot when I'm sitting at the front counter. The stool there is just so uncomfortable. It's one of those wooden ones with no cushion. I keep meaning to bring a pillow from home, but I always forget. I have this lovely needlepoint pillow my aunt made for me years ago. It has a picture of a little yellow canary on it. She loved birds, my aunt. She had three parakeets that used to fly right around her living room. They made such a mess, though, with the seeds everywhere. You'd step on them and they'd crunch into the carpet. 

Carpet is so hard to keep clean, don't you think? That's why we put laminate down in our hallway last year. It looks just like real oak, but you can just run a damp mop over it and you're done. My husband installed it himself. He's very handy like that, when his back isn't acting up. He threw it out last spring trying to lift a bag of mulch and was on the sofa for a week. 

But, oh, what were you asking? Fidgeting? I'm not really sure. I just... I like to keep my hands busy, I suppose.
Do you often find yourself interrupting other people when they are speaking?

Well, I... I suppose I do that, yes. Especially at the shop. I'll just cut right into my staff's conversations, or I'll reach over and start fixing how they're sorting the clothes before they even ask for help. I know it comes off like I'm butting in, but it's just... I see it being done wrong and I have to fix it. 

Like yesterday, Sarah was sorting a pile of silks, and she had this beautiful emerald green blouse right next to a rough wool cardigan. You can't do that! The wool will snag the silk in a heartbeat. Silk is so delicate. I had a silk scarf once, a real Hermes one that I found at an estate sale for five dollars. Can you believe it? Five dollars! The woman running the sale clearly had no idea what she had. It had this gorgeous equestrian print on it, all horses and riding crops. I wore it all the time until I accidentally left it in a taxi in Chicago. 

Chicago is so windy, though, isn't it? We went there for a long weekend a few years ago and I thought I was going to freeze. The pizza was good, though. Deep dish. It's really more like a casserole than a pizza, if you ask me. You need a knife and fork to eat it. 

But, um... interrupting. Right. Yes, I do that. I just can't seem to stop myself from jumping in when I see something that needs fixing or if I just have something to say right then.
